# Security policy

## Supported versions

Security fixes are applied to the current `main` branch only. Older commits and
tagged releases are not maintained separately. Update to the latest `main`
before checking whether a problem still occurs.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Use GitHub's private
[Report a vulnerability](https://github.com/hbeychaner/usa-congress-monitor/security/advisories/new)
form. You must be signed in to GitHub. Do not disclose vulnerabilities in public
issues, pull requests, discussions or wiki pages.

Include:

- The affected commit and component.
- A description of the issue and its potential impact.
- Minimal reproduction steps using your own local deployment or test data.
- Any suggested mitigation.

Do not include credentials, API keys, personal information or production data.
If a credential has been exposed, revoke or rotate it immediately; deleting it
from a file does not invalidate it.

Reports are handled on a best-effort basis, without a guaranteed response or
remediation timeline. Coordinate public disclosure privately with the
maintainer.

Only test systems you own or have permission to assess. Do not access other
people's data or disrupt running services.
